conditions.displayName: a container reports unhealthy or not running
health reporting stopped — absence is not health

documentation.content:
A container on the inflect-compliance VM is unhealthy or not running.

WHY THIS EXISTS (#2745). On 2026-09-20 production was down ~25h and nothing alerted. The /api/readyz uptime check now covers 'the app cannot serve'. This covers the other shape: UP BUT DOING NOTHING. A wedged BullMQ worker keeps its container running and the web tier green, so readyz stays 200 while no work happens at all.

WHAT THE SIGNAL MEANS. inflect-worker-1 reports unhealthy when the BullMQ heartbeat key goes stale — a key only a worker that PULLED A JOB, RAN IT and came back can write. It is not a process-existence check.

FIRST STEPS
1. gcloud compute ssh inflect-compliance --zone europe-west1-b
2. sudo docker ps -a    -- which container, and is it restarting?
3. sudo docker exec inflect-worker-1 node dist/worker-healthcheck.mjs
   exit 1 means the heartbeat is stale: a blocked event loop, a dropped Redis
   connection, every concurrency slot held, or a scheduler that never
   registered the 2-minute health-check repeatable.
4. sudo docker logs --tail 100 <container>

THE SECOND CONDITION IS THE REPORTER ITSELF. If the metric goes ABSENT the
reporter or its timer has died, and absence must never read as healthy:
  systemctl status container-health-reporter.timer
  sudo /usr/local/bin/container-health-reporter.sh

Docs: docs/runbooks/ (none yet for this), infra/alerts/external-uptime.yml
